```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## What a degree bound is here

A degree bound restricts how many components an actor may hold (its portfolio
size, the actor's outdegree in the bipartite network) or how many actors may
hold a component (the component's indegree). A floor of 1 on actors says that
no actor may be left holding nothing: an actor that wants to switch from
component A to component B must add B first and drop A afterwards. A cap says
that no actor may hold more than `max` components.

In SAOM-NK a bound is a **fixed modeling assumption**. It holds in forward
simulation and is imposed, unchanged, when the same model is estimated. It is
never an estimated parameter, and searchnet never reports an estimate for it.
The one exception is opt-in: an actor floor of 1 can instead be estimated as
the cost of dropping the last tie (`estimate_floor = TRUE`, described in
[its own section](#an-estimated-floor-the-cost-of-dropping-the-last-tie)
below), and it is then no longer a bound.

## How each bound is carried in RSiena

Everything below was verified on RSiena 1.5.0 with a two-mode dependent
network.

| Bound | RSiena mechanism | Exact? |
|---|---|---|
| actor max `k` | `MaxDegree = k` algorithm setting | exact: options above the cap are removed |
| actor min 1 | `outIso` (number of out-isolates), fixed at `-bound_penalty` | penalty |
| actor min `k > 1` | `outTrunc(k)` (sum of outdegrees truncated at `k`), fixed at `+bound_penalty` | penalty |
| component min 1, 2, 3 | `antiInIso` (+ `in2Plus`, + `in3Plus`), fixed at `+bound_penalty` | penalty |
| component max 1, 2 | `in2Plus` or `in3Plus`, fixed at `-bound_penalty` | penalty (barrier) |
| component min above 3, component max above 2 | none | **non-implementation** |

With the default `bound_penalty = 20`, a move across a penalized bound has a
choice probability of about `exp(-20)`, roughly 2e-9, relative to staying put.
The bound is therefore soft in principle, and searchnet checks it: every
simulated period ends with a gate that aborts the run if any bound was
crossed.

Two consequences of the penalty form are worth knowing.

* **A floor also attracts.** An actor below its floor gains `+20` by adding a
  component, so it adds one at its first opportunity. A start state below the
  floor would be repaired almost at once, but it would not satisfy the stated
  bounds, so searchnet stops by default and lists the violators.
  `repair_initial = TRUE` adds seeded random ties first instead, and says so.
* **A component cap is a barrier only.** The indicator `in3Plus` stops a
  component from gaining a third holder, but a component that already has four
  is not pulled back. A start state above any cap is always an error.

**Non-implementations.** RSiena 1.5.0 offers indegree indicators only up to
`in3Plus`, no indegree analogue of `outTrunc`, and `MaxDegree` applies to
outdegrees only. A component floor above 3 or a component cap above 2 is
refused with an error of class `"searchnet_not_implemented"`. That says
nothing about whether such a bound matters in the world; it says the software
offers no statistic for it.

**Maximum likelihood.** Estimation under bounds uses the method of moments.
RSiena 1.5.0 itself warns that `maxlike` and `MaxDegree` are incompatible, and
an ML fit of a bipartite network with `MaxDegree` stopped with a NaN score;
with only a fixed floor penalty, ML returned a missing standard error for a
period rate. searchnet refuses `maxlike = TRUE` whenever bounds are set.

## Declaring bounds

```{r declare}
library(searchnet)
b <- searchnet_degree_bounds(actor = c(min = 1, max = 3))
b
mod <- saomnk_model(density = -1.5, popularity = 0.1,
                    degree_bounds = c(min = 1, max = 3))
mod
```

The same `degree_bounds` argument is accepted by `searchnet_recovery()`,
`searchnet_coevolve()`, `run_calibrated_counterfactual()` and
`run_counterfactual_with_uncertainty()`.

A simulation under these bounds is an ordinary `saomnk_run()`:

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
env <- saomnk_env(M = 8, N = 6, density = 0.3, seed = 7)
saomnk_run(env, saomnk_model(density = -1.5, degree_bounds = c(min = 1, max = 3),
                             repair_initial = TRUE),
           steps_per_actor = 20, seed = 11)
range(apply(env$bi_env_arr, 3, rowSums))   # 1 3
```

## Checking observed data before estimation

Estimation under a bound assumes the bound held in every observed wave. A
method-of-moments fit cannot reproduce an observed degree the model forbids,
so a violating panel is an error before estimation, not a fit to report.
`searchnet_check_degree_bounds()` is called automatically by every estimation
entry point when bounds are set, and can be called directly:

```{r check}
B1 <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0,
               0, 1, 1), 2, 3, byrow = TRUE)
B2 <- B1; B2[1, 1] <- 0          # actor 1 drops its last component
try(searchnet_check_degree_bounds(list(B1, B2), c(min = 1)))
```

## Landscapes: infeasible portfolios

A landscape plot that enumerates all `2^N` portfolios of an actor would color
an infeasible portfolio by the fixed penalty, a utility near -20 that is a
modeling device rather than a payoff. `searchnet_portfolio_infeasible()` flags
those portfolios so a figure can grey them out:

```{r infeasible}
configs <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:1), 3)))
cbind(configs, infeasible = searchnet_portfolio_infeasible(configs, c(min = 1, max = 2)))
```

No existing figure changes: a plotting script opts in by calling it. The
README landscape script (`tools/make_readme_gif.R`) adds the flag to its JSON
only when its model carries bounds, which the README model does not.

## Choice probabilities under bounds

`env$compute_choice_probabilities()` reports, per actor, the logit
probabilities of each single toggle and of staying put. Under bounds it follows
the two mechanisms, which differ in kind:

* **An actor cap is a hard constraint.** `MaxDegree` removes the add options of
  an actor at the cap from its choice set, so they get probability exactly 0
  and the remaining toggles and the status quo are renormalized. Against
  RSiena's own simulated ministeps from a cap state, an actor never added and
  the frequency of staying put matched the renormalized probability within
  Monte Carlo error.
* **A floor or component cap is a fixed penalty.** The crossing move stays in
  the choice set with its weight multiplied by `exp(-20)`, as in the
  simulation; it is not set to 0, because the model is soft there.

Each element also carries `infeasible` (toggles that would leave any bound) and
`removed` (toggles `MaxDegree` removes). `renormalize = FALSE` returns the
unbounded formal-utility logit for comparison.

## Evidence: recovery with and without the bound

**What this section shows, and what it does not.** It shows recovery at one
design: M = 30 actors, N = 10 components, 3 waves, 100 replications, an actor
floor of 1, and the planted values below. Nothing more. It says nothing about
other sizes, densities, effects, or bounds.

The planted data-generating process has an actor floor of 1 (`outIso` fixed at
-20), `density = -1.8`, `inPop = 0.08` and a basic rate of 4 per period. Wave 1
is a Bernoulli draw at density 0.12, brought within the floor by seeded random
additions. Each simulated panel is estimated twice, on the same panels and
with the same seeds:

* **with the bound**: the panel is checked, `outIso` enters fixed at -20, and
  the method of moments estimates rate, `density` and `inPop`;
* **without the bound**: the same estimation with no `outIso` term, which is
  what an analyst who did not know about the floor would fit.

The runs take a few minutes, so the chunk that runs them is shown with
`eval = FALSE`. The printed output comes from results precomputed with exactly
that code by `tools/make_degree_bounds_vignette_data.R` and stored in
`inst/extdata/searchnet_degree_bounds_recovery.rds`.

```{r heavy, eval = FALSE}
design <- list(
  effects_spec = c("density", "inPop"),
  theta_true = c(rate = 4, density = -1.8, inPop = 0.08),
  M = 30L, N = 10L, waves = 3L, reps = 100L,
  nbrNodes = 1L, seed = 20261010L,
  n3 = 500L, nsub = 4L, init_density = 0.12,
  degree_bounds = c(min = 1),
  criterion = list(max_abs_bias = 0.10, min_coverage = 0.90,
                   min_converged_share = 0.90))
with_bounds    <- do.call(searchnet_recovery, c(design, list(estimate_with_bounds = TRUE)))
without_bounds <- do.call(searchnet_recovery, c(design, list(estimate_with_bounds = FALSE)))
```

```{r load}
path <- system.file("extdata", "searchnet_degree_bounds_recovery.rds",
                    package = "searchnet")
if (!nzchar(path))  # building from a source tree without an installed copy
  path <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "searchnet_degree_bounds_recovery.rds")
stored <- readRDS(path)
```

How often the floor binds in the simulated data (share of actors holding
exactly one component, share holding none, and mean portfolio size, by wave):

```{r binding}
round(stored$floor_binding, 3)
```

Estimated **with** the bound:

```{r with}
stored$with_bounds
```

Estimated **without** the bound, on the same panels:

```{r without}
stored$without_bounds
```

Side by side, for the two structural effects:

```{r compare}
pick <- function(x, arm) {
  t <- x$table[x$table$effect %in% c("density", "inPop"),
               c("effect", "true", "bias", "mcse_bias", "coverage", "rmse")]
  cbind(arm = arm, t)
}
cmp <- rbind(pick(stored$with_bounds, "with bound"),
             pick(stored$without_bounds, "without bound"))
num <- vapply(cmp, is.numeric, logical(1))
cmp[num] <- lapply(cmp[num], round, 3)
cmp
c(with_bound_seconds = stored$with_bounds$elapsed,
  without_bound_seconds = stored$without_bounds$elapsed)
```

**Reading.** The bias, coverage and verdict lines above are the result; the
criterion (absolute bias at most 0.10, coverage at least 0.90, at least 90
percent of replications converged) was fixed in the generating script before
the run. Omitting a floor that generated the data does not leave the model
merely less efficient: the estimator has to explain, through the remaining
effects, why actors at one component never drop it, and the effects it uses
for that absorb the bound. Which effects absorb it, and by how much, is
specific to this design.

## An estimated floor: the cost of dropping the last tie

A floor of 1 can be read two ways. As a definition (an actor exists only
while it holds something), it is a fixed assumption, as above. As a
behavior (actors are reluctant to drop their last component, but sometimes
do), it is a parameter to estimate. `estimate_floor = TRUE` takes the second
reading for a floor of 1:

```{r estimated-declare}
b_est <- searchnet_degree_bounds(actor = c(min = 1), estimate_floor = TRUE,
                                 floor_start = -2)
b_est
```

`outIso` then enters as a free evaluation effect. Its estimate is the cost of
dropping the last tie **relative to the other effects in the model**: how much
less an actor values holding nothing than those effects predict. It is not an
absolute quantity, and it moves when the rest of the specification moves.
Degree 0 is now allowed, so the floor drops out of the data check, the
simulation gates, the start-state repair and the infeasibility flags; any
other bound stays fixed.

A floor above 1 cannot be estimated this way. Its only carrier,
`outTrunc(k)`, has the same change statistic for every drop by an actor
holding `k` or fewer components, so a free coefficient measures how much more
the first `k` ties are worth than later ones, not the cost of crossing the
floor, and RSiena offers no outdegree indicator above `outIso`. searchnet
refuses it with an error of class `"searchnet_not_identified"`.

### Identification comes only from observed drops to degree 0

The method-of-moments target for `outIso` is the number of actors holding
nothing at the end of each period. If no actor is ever observed at degree 0,
the data say only that the cost is large, not how large: the estimate is not
identified and **only a bound can be reported**. That is a non-identification,
not a null. `searchnet_floor_identification()` counts the observed
transitions per wave and says which case applies:

```{r estimated-id}
B1 <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0,
               0, 1, 1,
               1, 1, 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
B2 <- B1; B2[1, 1] <- 0          # actor 1 drops its last component
searchnet_floor_identification(list(B1, B2))
searchnet_floor_identification(list(B1, B1))
```

The counts are net changes between waves: an actor that dropped its last
component and took another between two observations is not seen.

### Evidence: power and identification by the number of observed drops

**What this section shows, and what it does not.** It shows recovery of a
planted `outIso` at one family of designs: N = 8 components, 3 waves, a basic
rate of 3 per period, `density = -1` as the only other effect, wave 1 a
Bernoulli draw at density 0.2 with every actor brought to at least one
component, and 100 replications per cell. The planted `outIso` is 0, -1, -2 or
-4, and the number of actors M is 15, 30, 60 or 120; together they move how
many last-tie drops a panel shows. Every panel is estimated with `outIso`
free (starting at -2) by unconditional method of moments (`n3 = 500`,
`nsub = 4`, `nbrNodes = 1`). A panel with no observed drop to degree 0 is
filed as non-identified and not estimated. Nothing is shown about other
effects, sizes or densities.

The results come from `tools/make_floor_power_vignette_data.R` (about 40
minutes on one core under RSiena 1.5.0), which fixed the design and the
reading before the run, and are stored in
`inst/extdata/searchnet_floor_power.rds`. Each cell is the code below:

```{r estimated-heavy, eval = FALSE}
b <- searchnet_degree_bounds(actor = c(min = 1), estimate_floor = TRUE,
                             floor_start = -2)
rec <- searchnet_recovery("density",
                          theta_true = c(rate = 3, density = -1, outIso = -2),
                          reps = 100, M = 60, N = 8, waves = 3,
                          n3 = 500, nsub = 4, nbrNodes = 1,
                          init_density = 0.2, degree_bounds = b, seed = 20261022)
searchnet_floor_power(rec)
```

```{r estimated-load}
fpath <- system.file("extdata", "searchnet_floor_power.rds", package = "searchnet")
if (!nzchar(fpath))
  fpath <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "searchnet_floor_power.rds")
fp <- readRDS(fpath)
```

Per design cell: the median number of observed last-tie drops per panel, how
many panels had none (non-identified), and recovery over the converged ones.

```{r estimated-cells}
cells <- fp$by_cell
cells[] <- lapply(cells, function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) round(v, 3) else v)
cells[, c("outIso", "M", "median_drops", "n_non_identified", "n_converged",
          "bias", "coverage", "rejection", "mde")]
```

The minimum detectable effect by the observed count of drops, pooled over the
planted values (`mde` is `(z_0.975 + z_0.80)` times the mean standard error):

```{r estimated-mde}
mde <- fp$by_count[, c("drops", "drops_mean", "n_reps", "n_non_identified",
                       "n_converged", "mean_se", "mde")]
mde[] <- lapply(mde, function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) round(v, 2) else v)
mde
```

```{r estimated-mde-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "Minimum detectable outIso coefficient falling as the number of observed last-tie drops per panel rises"}
ok <- is.finite(fp$by_count$mde)
plot(fp$by_count$drops_mean[ok], fp$by_count$mde[ok], log = "x", type = "b",
     pch = 19, xlab = "observed last-tie drops per panel (bin mean, log scale)",
     ylab = "MDE of outIso (logit scale)", ylim = c(0, max(fp$by_count$mde[ok])),
     las = 1)
```

**Reading.** Four results, each conditional on this design.

* **Panels with no observed drop are common when the cost is large and the
  panel is small,** and they are counted as non-identified rather than
  dropped or read as nulls: 92 of 100 panels at `outIso = -4` with 15
  actors, 28 of 100 even with 120 actors.
* **Precision is governed by the count of drops.** The MDE falls from about
  2.7 with 1 to 4 observed drops to about 1.8 with 5 to 9, 1.4 with 10 to
  19, 1.0 with 20 to 39 and 0.8 with 40 or more. With fewer than 5 drops only
  a reluctance near 3 on the logit scale would be detected reliably.
* **Size is controlled.** With nothing planted (`outIso = 0`), rejection of
  `outIso = 0` stays between 0 and 0.06 in every cell.
* **Recovery is close where few panels are non-identified, and biased toward
  zero where many are.** At `outIso = -4` with 15 or 30 actors the converged
  panels are the minority that happened to show drops, and their estimates
  are less negative than the planted value (bias +2.5 and +1.4). That is
  selection on the outcome that identifies the parameter, not an estimator
  failure; the same selection makes the bias and coverage columns of
  `searchnet_floor_power()` conditional summaries, to be read with that in
  mind. Report the share of non-identified panels with any estimate.
